sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: A circular oil spill is expanding so that its radius increases at $3$ m/min. How fast is the area increasing when the radius is $50$ m?
A 10 m ladder leans against a wall. The bottom slides away from the wall at $2$ m/s. How fast is the top sliding down when the bottom is $6$ m from the wall?
questions.answer: $x^2 + y^2 = 100$. Differentiating: $2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$. At $x=6$, $y=8$: $12(2) + 16\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$, so $\frac{dy}{dt} = -1.5$ m/s (the top is sliding down at $1.5$ m/s).
questions.explanation: $x^2 + y^2 = 100$. Differentiating: $2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$. At $x=6$, $y=8$: $12(2) + 16\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$, so $\frac{dy}{dt} = -1.5$ m/s (the top is sliding down at $1.5$ m/s).

questions.q: Air is pumped into a spherical balloon at $100$ cm$^3$/s. Find the rate of change of the radius when $r = 5$ cm, to three decimal places.

Water drains from a conical tank (vertex down) with radius 4 m and height 10 m at the top, at a rate of $2$ m$^3$/min. Using similar triangles $r = \frac{2h}{5}$, find how fast the water level is dropping when $h = 5$ m.
questions.answer: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi\left(\frac{2h}{5}\right)^2 h = \frac{4\pi}{75}h^3$. So $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{12\pi}{75}h^2\frac{dh}{dt}$. At $h=5$: $-2 = \frac{12\pi}{75}(25)\frac{dh}{dt}$, giving $\frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{2 \times 75}{300\pi} = -\frac{1}{2\pi} \approx -0.159$ m/min.
questions.explanation: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi\left(\frac{2h}{5}\right)^2 h = \frac{4\pi}{75}h^3$. So $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{12\pi}{75}h^2\frac{dh}{dt}$. At $h=5$: $-2 = \frac{12\pi}{75}(25)\frac{dh}{dt}$, giving $\frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{2 \times 75}{300\pi} = -\frac{1}{2\pi} \approx -0.159$ m/min.

questions.q: A camera tracks a rocket launching vertically, 500 m from the launch pad. When the rocket is 1200 m high and rising at 200 m/s, how fast is the camera's angle of elevation increasing? Give the answer in radians/s, to four decimal places.
Two cars leave an intersection at the same time, one heading north at 40 mph and the other heading east at 30 mph. How fast is the distance between them increasing after 2 hours?
questions.answer: $x=60$ mi, $y=80$ mi (east, north after 2 h). $s^2=x^2+y^2$: $2s\frac{ds}{dt}=2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}$. $s=100$: $100\frac{ds}{dt}=60(30)+80(40)=1800+3200=5000$, so $\frac{ds}{dt}=50$ mph.
questions.explanation: $x=60$ mi, $y=80$ mi (east, north after 2 h). $s^2=x^2+y^2$: $2s\frac{ds}{dt}=2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}$. $s=100$: $100\frac{ds}{dt}=60(30)+80(40)=1800+3200=5000$, so $\frac{ds}{dt}=50$ mph.

questions.q: A streetlight is 6 m high. A 1.8 m tall person walks away from it at 1.5 m/s. Using similar triangles, find how fast the length of the person's shadow is growing.
questions.answer: Let $x$ = distance from pole, $s$ = shadow length. Similar triangles: $\frac{6}{x+s}=\frac{1.8}{s}$, so $6s=1.8x+1.8s$, giving $4.2s=1.8x$, $s=\frac{1.8}{4.2}x=\frac{3}{7}x$. $\frac{ds}{dt}=\frac{3}{7}\cdot1.5\approx0.643$ m/s.
questions.explanation: Let $x$ = distance from pole, $s$ = shadow length. Similar triangles: $\frac{6}{x+s}=\frac{1.8}{s}$, so $6s=1.8x+1.8s$, giving $4.2s=1.8x$, $s=\frac{1.8}{4.2}x=\frac{3}{7}x$. $\frac{ds}{dt}=\frac{3}{7}\cdot1.5\approx0.643$ m/s.

questions.q: The volume of a cube is increasing at $12$ cm$^3$/s. Find the rate of change of the side length when the side is $3$ cm.

A kite is flying at a constant height of 40 m, moving horizontally away from the person holding the string at 3 m/s. Find the rate at which the string length is increasing when the kite is 30 m horizontally from the person.

A conical pile of sand has its height always equal to its base radius. Sand is added at $10$ m$^3$/min. Find the rate of change of the height when $h=5$ m, using $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\frac{1}{3}\pi h^3$.

The graph shows $A(r)=\pi r^2$, the area of the oil spill from the first problem, as a function of radius alone (not time). Explain why $\frac{dA}{dt}$ still depends on $\frac{dr}{dt}$ even though this graph has no time axis.
questions.answer: The graph shows how $A$ depends on $r$, but $r$ itself changes with time. The chain rule $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}=2\pi r\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}$ combines the graph's slope ($\frac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r$) with the given rate $\frac{dr}{dt}$ to produce the actual rate of change over time.
questions.explanation: The graph shows how $A$ depends on $r$, but $r$ itself changes with time. The chain rule $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}=2\pi r\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}$ combines the graph's slope ($\frac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r$) with the given rate $\frac{dr}{dt}$ to produce the actual rate of change over time.

questions.q: For the same rectangle (length $=2\times$ width), find the rate of change of the perimeter when the width is increasing at $3$ cm/s.
questions.target: Related rates with area and perimeter together
questions.answer: $P=2(w+2w)=6w$. $\frac{dP}{dt}=6\frac{dw}{dt}=6(3)=18$ cm/s (constant, independent of $w$, since $P$ is linear in $w$).
questions.explanation: $P=2(w+2w)=6w$. $\frac{dP}{dt}=6\frac{dw}{dt}=6(3)=18$ cm/s (constant, independent of $w$, since $P$ is linear in $w$).

questions.q: The radius of a circle expands at a constant rate of $3\mathrm{\ cm/s}$. How fast is the area increasing when the radius is $10\mathrm{\ cm}$?
Air is pumped into a spherical balloon so that its volume increases at $100\mathrm{\ cm}^3\mathrm{/s}$. How fast is the radius increasing when $r = 5\mathrm{\ cm}$?
The edge length $s$ of a cube increases at $2\mathrm{\ cm/s}$. At what rate is the surface area increasing when $s = 4\mathrm{\ cm}$?

A $13\mathrm{-ft}$ ladder leans against a vertical wall. If the bottom slides away from the wall at $2\mathrm{\ ft/s}$, how fast is the top sliding down when the bottom is $5\mathrm{\ ft}$ from the wall?
Two cars start from the same point. Car A travels north at $40\mathrm{\ mph}$ and Car B travels east at $30\mathrm{\ mph}$. How fast is the distance between them increasing after 2 hours?
questions.answer: After 2 h: $y = 80\mathrm{\ miles}, x = 60\mathrm{\ miles}, z = \sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = 100\mathrm{\ miles}$. $2z\frac{dz}{dt} = 2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} \Rightarrow 100\frac{dz}{dt} = 60(30) + 80(40) = 1800 + 3200 = 5000 \Rightarrow \frac{dz}{dt} = 50\mathrm{\ mph}$.
questions.explanation: After 2 h: $y = 80\mathrm{\ miles}, x = 60\mathrm{\ miles}, z = \sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = 100\mathrm{\ miles}$. $2z\frac{dz}{dt} = 2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} \Rightarrow 100\frac{dz}{dt} = 60(30) + 80(40) = 1800 + 3200 = 5000 \Rightarrow \frac{dz}{dt} = 50\mathrm{\ mph}$.

questions.q: In the 13-ft ladder problem ($x = 5, y = 12, dx/dt = 2$), at what rate is the area of the triangle formed by the ladder changing?
Water flows into an inverted conical tank (radius $4\mathrm{\ m}$, height $12\mathrm{\ m}$) at $2\mathrm{\ m}^3\mathrm{/min}$. How fast is the water level rising when the depth is $6\mathrm{\ m}$?
questions.answer: By similar triangles, $r/h = 4/12 = 1/3 \Rightarrow r = h/3$. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(h/3)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{27}h^3$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{9}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. At $h = 6$: $2 = \frac{\pi}{9}(36)\frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{2}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\mathrm{\ m/min}$.
questions.explanation: By similar triangles, $r/h = 4/12 = 1/3 \Rightarrow r = h/3$. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(h/3)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{27}h^3$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{9}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. At $h = 6$: $2 = \frac{\pi}{9}(36)\frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{2}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\mathrm{\ m/min}$.

sections.heading: Part V — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Application (29–37)

questions.q: A trough with triangular cross-section (base $2\mathrm{\ m}$, depth $2\mathrm{\ m}$, length $6\mathrm{\ m}$) leaks water at $0.5\mathrm{\ m}^3\mathrm{/min}$. What is $dh/dt$ when $h = 1\mathrm{\ m}$?
questions.answer: Cross section base $b = h$. $V = \frac{1}{2}b h \times 6 = 3h^2$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = 6h \frac{dh}{dt}$. $-0.5 = 6(1)\frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{0.5}{6} = -\frac{1}{12}\mathrm{\ m/min}$.
questions.explanation: Cross section base $b = h$. $V = \frac{1}{2}b h \times 6 = 3h^2$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = 6h \frac{dh}{dt}$. $-0.5 = 6(1)\frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{0.5}{6} = -\frac{1}{12}\mathrm{\ m/min}$.

questions.answer: Tip position is $x + s = x + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{5}{3}x$. Rate of tip $= \frac{5}{3}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{5}{3}(4) = \frac{20}{3}\mathrm{\ ft/s}$.
questions.explanation: Tip position is $x + s = x + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{5}{3}x$. Rate of tip $= \frac{5}{3}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{5}{3}(4) = \frac{20}{3}\mathrm{\ ft/s}$.
